start.title: Check your room's <nw>Wi-Fi</nw> and devices
start.intro: Find out what's connected, who else might control it, and whether the Wi-Fi can be trusted. About {{minutes}} minutes.

demo.title: Demo mode: made-up data, nothing is scanned
demo.body: Every check here shows made-up results for the network “Example-Home”. Nothing on your network is checked, and nothing is sent anywhere. Run RoomCheck without --demo for a real check.

checks.devices: Devices on this network that look like cameras, smart locks, speakers or other connected devices.
checks.router: How the router and the network are set up, for example how the Wi-Fi is encrypted.
checks.nearby: Nearby Wi-Fi networks that copy your network's name, and Bluetooth trackers.

ready.label: Is this laptop ready?
ready.failed: Couldn't check this laptop's setup. You can still start a check.
ready.noneFix: Connect to the room's Wi-Fi first, then choose “Check again”.

differentBody.one: RoomCheck checks the network this laptop is connected to.
differentBody.two: To switch, open Quick Settings (Windows key + A), choose Wi-Fi, and connect to the room's network.
differentBody.three: Then choose “Check again”. RoomCheck never changes Windows settings itself.

wifi.name: Wi-Fi radio
wifi.fix: Turn on Wi-Fi in Quick Settings (Windows key + A).

bluetooth.name: Bluetooth
bluetooth.fix: Turn on Bluetooth in Quick Settings (Windows key + A).

location.name: Windows Location
location.fix: Open Settings, then Privacy & security, then Location. Turn on Location services and “Let desktop apps access your location”.

npcap.name: Npcap
npcap.fix: Install the free Npcap driver from npcap.com, then restart RoomCheck.

nmap.name: Nmap
nmap.fix: Install Nmap from nmap.org, then restart RoomCheck. Only a full check uses it.

ready.recheckFailed: Couldn't check again. Try once more.

permission.legend: Do you have permission to check this network?
permission.hint: Being on the Wi-Fi isn't the same as permission.
permission.legal: Checking devices on a network without permission may be against the law in many places.

whatCountsBody.said: its owner or your host has said yes, ideally in writing.
whatCountsBody.advice: This isn't legal advice. If you're not sure, choose “No, or I'm not sure” and RoomCheck will only listen.

permission.yesHint: Also checks what each device runs, as well as announced signals.
permission.noHint: RoomCheck only listens. You can ask your host for permission.

start.footer: Results are clues, not proof. Everything runs on this laptop. <cant>What it can't see</cant> and <sent>what's sent</sent>
start.startFailed: The check couldn't start. Make sure RoomCheck is still running, then try again.

trust.limitation: Results are clues, not proof. Some devices won't be detected.

cant.offline: It can't see devices that record to a memory card and never connect to a network.
cant.where: It can't say exactly where a device is. It only knows it's on this network or nearby.
cant.login: It never logs in to anything or changes any setting, so some details stay unknown.

trust.networkName: The network name on Start is shown on this laptop only and is never sent anywhere.

stay.hint: It changes some next steps, such as who to report a camera to.
stay.rentalDescription: A room or a whole flat rented from a host
stay.hostelDescription: A hostel or other shared accommodation
stay.otherDescription: Anywhere else. The next steps stay general.

privacy.intro: Everything runs on this laptop. Only these optional calls go out:

ai.when: off unless you add an Anthropic API key
ai.sent: send each finding's rule and wording, with the device type and maker. Never addresses, device names or network names.

nvd.sent: product names are sent to NIST's vulnerability database.

tsa.when: on by default when you make a report; you can turn them off
tsa.sent: only the report's fingerprint (hash) is sent to freetsa.org.

privacy.aiOn: AI is on in this setup
privacy.aiOff: AI is off in this setup

report.title: Handover report
report.intro: A PDF of your latest check, with a fingerprint, and a trusted timestamp if you choose one.
report.roomLabelHint: Shown at the top of the report, for example “Room 4B”.

report.timestampAt: Signed by the FreeTSA timestamp service at {{when}}.

report.verifiedNot: This PDF doesn't match its timestamp.
report.verifyFailed: The timestamp can't be verified just now. You can verify it later on the Verify page.

deleteAll.question: Delete all saved RoomCheck data from this laptop? This deletes your move-in scan, your handover tasks with their statuses and notes, your answers to “Do you recognise this device?”, the names and notes you gave devices, and the key used to match devices between checks. It can't be recovered. Reports you've already saved as files aren't affected.

help.title: Help
help.cameraTitle: If you find a hidden camera

camera.touch: Don't touch or unplug it. Photograph it where it is.
camera.report: Report it to the police, and to whoever runs the place: the platform, the host or landlord's agent, or the management.
camera.note: Many platforms don't allow indoor cameras; Airbnb hasn't since 2024. Laws differ by country. This isn't legal advice.

priority.fixed: Each finding's priority comes from a fixed rule in RoomCheck, the same every time.
priority.levels: From most to least urgent: Look at this first, Look at this soon, Worth knowing, For information.
priority.ai: The AI only words the explanations. It never sets or changes a priority.

saved.key: A random key that matches the same devices between checks.

help.where: It's all in %LOCALAPPDATA%\RoomCheck, encrypted for your Windows account. Nothing is sent anywhere.
help.reports: Reports are files in %LOCALAPPDATA%\RoomCheck\reports. Deleting your data doesn't remove them: delete those files yourself.

permission.title: Ask your host for permission
permission.intro: Permission in writing lets you run a check with permission next time. RoomCheck never sends anything: edit the message if you like, copy it and send it yourself.
permission.message:
Hello,

I'd like to check the devices on the Wi-Fi where I'm staying, using an app called RoomCheck on my own laptop. With your permission, it would ask the devices on the network which services they offer. It doesn't log in to anything, try passwords or change any settings.

Could you reply to say whether that's OK?

Thank you.
permission.note: Keep the reply. It's your permission in writing.

physical.title: Do a 3-minute physical check
physical.intro: Look at these places with your own eyes and your phone's torch. Tick each one you've looked at, and note anything you're not sure about.
physical.offerBody: Some cameras send nothing a network check can hear. A quick look around covers what these checks can't.

items.facing_bed: Anything facing the bed, shower or toilet
items.lenses: Small holes or lenses that catch a phone torch

hints.smoke_detector: Look for a small lens or a light that doesn't belong.
hints.chargers: Check any you didn't bring, especially ones facing the bed.
hints.clocks: Look at the face and the edges for a small hole or lens.
hints.tv_box: Look around the screen's edges and the front of the box.
hints.purifier_speaker: Look at the grilles and vents.
hints.facing_bed: Anything pointed at where you sleep or wash.
hints.mirrors: Turn off the lights and hold your phone's torch against the glass. If you can see through to a space behind it, note it. It's a check, not proof.
hints.lenses: Turn the lights off and sweep your phone torch slowly. A lens shines back as a small glint.

physical.doneText: Done. Note anything you weren't sure about.
physical.focusIntro: For the {{label}}: the places most likely to hide one are listed first.

platformReport.intro: A message you can send through the platform's help centre. RoomCheck never sends anything: edit it if you like, copy it and send it yourself.
platformReport.message:
Hello,

I'm staying at a listing I booked through you. I found a device inside the room or unit that may be a camera. I've photographed it where it is and haven't touched it.

Could you look into this, and tell me what I should do next?

Thank you.
platformReport.note: Keep a copy of what you send, and your photos.
